name: Mountain (Kavkazi)
aliases: Tats (Soviet-era misnomer; per EJE, 17,109 Mountain Jews in the 1970 census and about 22,000 in 1979 called themselves Tats to avoid being registered as Jews)

database_scope.purpose: Sourced reference for Mountain (Kavkazi) minhagim and halachic practice. It records what the cited sources say, with a confidence level for each entry, and is not a psak.
database_scope.coverage_note: 30 sourced topics and 7 distinctive customs, compiled from the cited sources in October 2026. Each entry carries a confidence level (well-attested, disputed, regional, needs-review). 13 topics have no community-specific source and are listed under 'gaps' rather than filled with generic text.

identity.primary_origin: The eastern Caucasus: Dagestan (Derbent) and northern Azerbaijan (Quba)

languages: Juhuri: the community's language; the Haggadah is read in Juhuri translation at the second seder, and the first Juhuri books were printed in Vilna in 1908-1909

subgroups.name: Dagestan (Derbent, Makhachkala/Petrovsk, Buynaksk/Temir-Khan-Shura, Khasavyurt, former villages Majalis, Nyugdi, Mamrach)
subgroups.note: Derbent was the seat of the Mountain Jewish chief rabbinate (R. Eliyahu b. Mishael, then the Yitzchaki dynasty), recognised for southern Dagestan and Azerbaijan.

subgroups.name: Azerbaijan (Quba / Krasnaya Sloboda / Qirmizi Qesebe, Baku, Oghuz/Vartashen)
subgroups.note: Krasnaya Sloboda was a federation of quarter-communities by place of origin, each with its own synagogue and rabbis. Vartashen is the best-documented community for 19th-century festival ritual (Bezhanov, 1894).

subgroups.name: North Caucasus (Nalchik/Kabardino-Balkaria, Grozny/Chechnya, Pyatigorsk, Kizlyar)
subgroups.note: The northern district rabbinate sat in Temir-Khan-Shura. Grozny's synagogue was confiscated in 1963 and the community dispersed in the 1990s. Few Grozny-specific customs are documented.

subgroups.name: Diaspora (Israel, Brooklyn, Moscow, Toronto, Germany)
subgroups.note: Brooklyn: Kavkazi Jewish Congregation / Beit Knesset Ohr haMizrah, Ocean Parkway (opened 2001). Israel: Hadera, Kiryat Yam, Be'er Ya'akov; Jerusalem synagogue Ohel Yona.

timeline.event: Venice-printed books reach the Caucasus; in Quba, books printed in Venice in the late 16th and early 17th c. were kept until the early 20th c. (EJE).
timeline.halachic_impact: A lost local manuscript nusach was displaced by the Sephardi nusach, still used today (Dymshits 1999; EJE 'Горские евреи').

timeline.event: Local works: piyyutim of Elisha b. Shmuel of Aba-Sava; R. Gershon Lala's Rambam commentary; R. Mattatiah b. Shmuel Mizrachi of Shemakha's kabbalistic 'Kol Mevaser' (1806-1828).
timeline.halachic_impact: Little local halachic literature; higher authority came from Iran, Iraq and Eretz Israel.

timeline.event: R. Eliyahu b. Mishael founds the Derbent chief rabbinate, studies in Jerusalem and Baghdad, and sends students to Belaya Tserkov in the late 1820s.
timeline.halachic_impact: Standardised liturgy; start of Ashkenazi-yeshiva training for Mountain Jewish rabbis.

timeline.event: Russian authorities recognise the Derbent chief rabbis as crown rabbis; two districts (south: Derbent; north: Temir-Khan-Shura).
timeline.halachic_impact: Chief rabbis act as dayanim and train shochtim and moelim; the village 'rabbi' is mainly shochet, mohel, melamed and chazzan.

timeline.event: Machzor Ohalei Yaakov printed in Jerusalem; first Juhuri books printed in Vilna (1908 'Zionism'; 1909 siddur 'Kol Tefilla' with parallel Hebrew, tr. Asaf Pinkhasov).
timeline.halachic_impact: A community-authored High Holiday machzor; the first vernacular siddur.

timeline.event: Soviet synagogue closures and repression of rabbis; by perestroika six synagogues remained (Baku, Quba, Derbent, Buynaksk, Makhachkala, Nalchik), and Oghuz reopened in 1994.
timeline.halachic_impact: Practice survived mainly in life-cycle and home ritual; festival meanings sometimes shifted to folk explanations.

timeline.event: Mass emigration to Israel, the US and Moscow. American Gorski leaders put their own community at 10,000-20,000, mostly in Brooklyn, with smaller groups in Detroit and Pennsylvania (Hadassah 2008).
timeline.halachic_impact: Diaspora communities may follow outside rabbinic leadership while keeping their own customs. Brooklyn's official rabbi is Yosef Elishevitz, 'a Lubavitch of Ashkenazic origin'; 'our elders tell him our customs, and he accommodates our traditions' (Hadassah 2008). Selected customs (rice, Govgil) persist.

primary_codes: Shulchan Aruch as the general Sephardi baseline; R. Bentsion Zilber explicitly treats the Mountain Jewish community as 'part of Sephardi society' when applying it to Omer practice
major_rishonim_base: No community-specific rishon documented; an 18th-c. commentary on Rambam's Mishneh Torah by R. Gershon Lala b. Moshe Nakdi of Aba-Sava is recorded (Dymshits 1999)
later_poskim: Chida (R. Chaim Yosef David Azulai): his order of prayers was introduced in all communities by R. Eliyahu b. Mishael (per Davidov)
R. Eliyahu b. Mishael of Derbent (1781-1848), first chief rabbi
R. Yitzchak b. Yaakov (1795-1877), dayan and chief rabbi of Derbent
R. Yaakov Yitzchaki (1846-1917), chief rabbi of Derbent, author of Machzor Ohalei Yaakov (Jerusalem 1908, 1910) and responsa
R. Hizgil b. Avraham Mishailov, northern-district chief rabbi (Temir-Khan-Shura, 1885-1904)
core_halachic_authorities.decision_principle: Documented practice combines a Sephardi liturgical base (imported Venice/Livorno printed books; the Chida's prayer order) with local minhag passed down orally through family and community ritual ('orthopraxy, not orthodoxy', Dymshits). Hadassah Magazine (2008) says the community 'had earlier sent their rabbinical students to Baghdad, began to send them to Lithuanian yeshivot—albeit without adopting Ashkenazic customs.' Where custom and Shulchan Aruch differ, contemporary rabbis (e.g. R. Zilber on Omer weddings) have accepted the inherited custom.

runtime.practice_baseline: Sephardi-rite practice resting on the Shulchan Aruch and the Chida's prayer order as introduced by the Derbent rabbinate, overlaid with distinct Caucasian community minhagim.

halacha_index.summary: Mountain Jews pray in the Sephardi rite. An earlier local manuscript nusach did not survive; it was replaced by Sephardi books printed in Venice and Livorno (c. late 16th-early 17th c.). R. Eliyahu b. Mishael instituted the Chida's prayer order in all communities.
common_practices: Sephardi siddur; Vilna-printed books used alongside Livorno ones after annexation
The rabbi leads aloud; less literate worshippers answer 'Baruch hu u-varuch shemo' and 'Amen'

variants.practice: A congregant's grandfather's siddur was a Turkish-printed Sephardi siddur with Ladino instructions (per adviser R. Moshe Scharhon).
Machzor Ohalei Yaakov by R. Yaakov Yitzchaki, described by a reprint seller as nusach Edot HaMizrach.

halacha_index.source: V. Dymshits (ed.), Gorskie evrei: istoriya, etnografiya, kul'tura (DAAT/Znanie, 1999), ch. 'Religioznaya zhizn' i obychai' (Russian); A. Davidov, Mudretsy Kavkaza, 'Nastavniki i uchitelya' (Russian); EJE (ORT), 'Горские евреи'
halacha_index.review_notes: The Chida attribution rests on Davidov alone. An Aish.com claim of a separate 'Nusach Kavkazi' has no scholarly support and is not adopted here.

halacha_index.summary_he: יהודי ההרים מתפללים בנוסח ספרד. נוסח כתב יד מקומי קדום יותר לא שרד; הוא הוחלף בספרים ספרדיים שנדפסו בוונציה ובליוורנו (בערך סוף המאה ה-16 ותחילת ה-17). רבי אליהו בן מיכאל קבע בכל הקהילות את סדר התפילה של החיד"א.

halacha_index.summary: The synagogue is called 'nimaz'. Traditionally there was no women's gallery; worshippers sat on carpets. The ark (heikhal) is on the western wall and the teva in the centre. Women came on Yom Kippur and stood at the entrance and windows.
common_practices: Carpets; formerly floor seating, now benches

variants.practice: Visitors were asked to remove shoes before entering.
variants.source: Intermountain Jewish News, 'Letter from Azerbaijan' (single journalistic observation)

variants.practice: Rugs in sanctuary and beit midrash; main sanctuary unused on weekdays.

halacha_index.source: Dymshits 1999 (citing Anisimov); Davidov, 'Chtenie Tory' (Russian)
halacha_index.review_notes: Shoe removal comes from a single journalistic report and is unverified.

Чтение Торы (Обычаи и традиции) / Главы / Библиотека / Еврейская интернет библиотека

halacha_index.summary_he: בית הכנסת נקרא "נימאז". במסורת לא הייתה עזרת נשים; המתפללים ישבו על שטיחים. ארון הקודש (היכל) בקיר המערבי והתיבה במרכז. נשים באו ביום כיפור ועמדו בכניסה ובחלונות.

halacha_index.summary: The Torah scroll wears two soft covers, an inner one of white cloth and an outer one of velvet or silk, and is read lying on a table. Rimonim act as the crown; no keter is used. Two silver pointers joined by a chain are held like a divider.
common_practices: Seven aliyot plus maftir are bought; mourners' relatives have priority
The oleh names deceased relatives for El Male Rachamim
The congregation repeats the haftarah blessings after the maftir
Go up to the bimah on the right, down on the left

variants.practice: Torah described as kept in a gilded wooden case.

halacha_index.source: Dymshits 1999, 'Ritual'naya utvar''; Davidov, 'Chtenie Tory (Obychai i traditsii)' (Russian)
halacha_index.review_notes: Dymshits calls the double soft cover unique among Jewish communities. For trope, see gaps.

halacha_index.summary_he: ספר התורה לבוש שני כיסויים רכים, פנימי מבד לבן וחיצוני ממשי קטיפה או משי, ונקרא כשהוא מונח על שולחן. הרימונים משמשים כתר; לא משתמשים בכתר. שתי ידות כסף המחוברות בשרשרת מוחזקות כמו מחוגה.

halacha_index.topic: Motzaei Shabbat: night of Elijah (Shev Ileh-Novi)
halacha_index.summary: The night after Shabbat is 'Shev Ileh-Novi', the night of Elijah the Prophet. Wives cooked khinkal in case Elijah came as a poor guest; folk belief held that whoever hosted him would grow rich.
common_practices: Cooking khinkal after Shabbat
halacha_index.source: Dymshits 1999, 'Verovaniya, obychai, obryady', quoting I. Anisimov (1888) (Russian)
halacha_index.review_notes: A 19th-century folk custom with a single source; it is ethnography, not halacha. Other Shabbat topics: see gaps.
halacha_index.summary_he: הלילה שאחרי שבת הוא "שב אילה-נבי", ליל אליהו הנביא. נשים בישלו חינקל למקרה שאליהו יבוא כאורח עני; אמונה עממית גרסה שמי שיארח אותו יתעשר.

halacha_index.summary: Chickens and rams are slaughtered the day before. In the evening there is a ram's head, pumpkin and fish, with dates, honey, carrot and apple after the evening prayer, and blessings over wine and all the foods. After the meal, half of Tehillim is said; by day Tehillim twice through, and Mishnah at night. People avoid sleeping. Tashlich is at the river, shaking the edges of garments.
common_practices: Ram's head, pumpkin, fish, dates, honey, carrot, apple
Tashlich at a river

variants.practice: One fast day before and one after the festival.

halacha_index.source: Dymshits 1999, 'Rosh a-Shana', quoting Bezhanov (1894) (Russian)
halacha_index.review_notes: Bezhanov was an outside observer who leaves out the shofar (Dymshits).
halacha_index.summary_he: שוחטים תרנגולות ואיילים יום לפני כן. בערב יש ראש איל, דלעת ודג, עם תמרים, דבש, גזר ותפוח אחרי תפילת הערב, וברכות על יין ועל כל המאכלים. אחרי הסעודה אומרים חצי מהתהילים; ביום תהילים פעמיים, ומשנה בלילה. נמנעים משינה. התשליך בנהר, תוך ניעור שולי הבגדים.

halacha_index.summary: Yom Kippur ('Kyupyur') is the most revered day, with the highest synagogue attendance even under Soviet rule. Kapparot is performed. Before the pre-fast meal, a candle is lit at home for each household member and for deceased relatives, especially parents. At the end of the fast, all kiss the rabbi's hand and the young kiss the elders' hands, asking forgiveness.
common_practices: Kapparot with a fowl per person
Household and memorial candles

variants.practice: A very large candle and 50 small ones lit in the synagogue; many stay all night.
A white garment hung on the bimah for the rabbi to wear on Yom Kippur.

halacha_index.source: Dymshits 1999, 'Iom Kipur' (Russian); Encyclopedia of World Cultures, 'Mountain Jews'
halacha_index.review_notes: Dymshits links the candles to Nowruz practice; this is an interpretation.

references.title: Религиозная жизнь и обычаи горских евреев / Главы / Библиотека / Еврейская интернет библиотека
Mountain Jews | Encyclopedia.com

halacha_index.summary_he: יום כיפור ("קיופיור") הוא היום הנערץ ביותר, עם הנוכחות הגבוהה ביותר בבית הכנסת אפילו בשלטון הסובייטי. מקיימים כפרות. לפני הסעודה המפסקת מדליקים בבית נר לכל בן בית ולקרובים שנפטרו, בייחוד להורים. בסוף הצום כולם מנשקים את יד הרב והצעירים מנשקים את ידי הזקנים, ומבקשים סליחה.

halacha_index.summary: The sukkah is now built in the synagogue courtyard. Formerly each courtyard had one, using the arbor ('chordog') or a booth with carpet walls and branches on top. Kiddush is made in the sukkah.
common_practices: Marking the sukkah site with a stick after Yom Kippur (Vartashen)

variants.practice: Kiddush in the sukkah, but people did not stay in it all day.
Supper in the sukkah; 'they live seven days in the sukkah'.

halacha_index.source: Dymshits 1999, 'Sukkot' (Russian)
halacha_index.review_notes: The sources disagree on how much time was spent in the sukkah.
halacha_index.summary_he: הסוכה נבנית היום בחצר בית הכנסת. בעבר הייתה אחת בכל חצר, בגפן הסוכך ("חורדוג") או בסוכה עם קירות שטיחים וענפים על גביה. עושים קידוש בסוכה.

halacha_index.summary: Hoshana Rabba is called 'Aravo' (willow) and is specially honoured. Willows are brought to the synagogue, then taken home and kept for a year. Men read Tehillim all night in the synagogue; the night is believed to seal one's fate.
common_practices: Keeping the aravot for a year
All-night Tehillim

variants.practice: Girls held all-night gatherings with dance, song contests and fortune-telling.

halacha_index.source: Dymshits 1999, 'Sukkot' (Russian)
halacha_index.review_notes: The girls' divination is folk custom.
halacha_index.summary_he: הושענא רבה נקרא "אראבו" (ערבה) ומכובד במיוחד. מביאים ערבות לבית הכנסת, אחר כך לוקחים אותן הביתה ושומרים אותן שנה. גברים אומרים תהילים כל הלילה בבית הכנסת; מאמינים שבלילה זה נחתם הגורל.

halacha_index.summary: Sources disagree. Dymshits found Chanukah not specially honoured, and most informants could not recall it. The Encyclopedia of World Cultures calls 'Khanukoi' the major winter holiday.

variants.practice: Barely remembered by elderly informants.
'Khanukoi' as the major winter holiday.

halacha_index.source: Dymshits 1999 (Russian); Encyclopedia of World Cultures via Encyclopedia.com
halacha_index.review_notes: No distinctive lighting custom is documented.

references.title: Религиозная жизнь и обычаи горских евреев / Главы / Библиотека / Еврейская интернет библиотека

halacha_index.summary_he: המקורות חלוקים. דימשיץ מצא שחנוכה אינו מכובד במיוחד, ורוב המשיבים לא זכרו אותו. האנציקלופדיה של תרבויות העולם קוראת ל"חנוקוי" חג החורף הגדול.

halacha_index.summary: Purim is one of the most popular festivals; its names come from Haman. On the Fast of Esther, women prepare 'hasido' halva (roasted flour, butter, honey or sugar, nuts) and thin lavash. The evening meal is 'kute heshil' flour soup with honey, with relatives invited and meals sent to the needy.
common_practices: Hasido halva
Food sent to the poor
Children born on Purim named Ester, Purim or Mordechai

variants.practice: Children carve a Haman figure on a board and beat it until it is erased, stamping, with music.
Called 'Hamano'; 'hadassoh' flour-and-honey halva instead of hamentaschen.

halacha_index.source: gorskie.ru 2016 (Russian); Dymshits 1999; Encyclopedia of World Cultures
halacha_index.review_notes: gorskie.ru reports that the traveller Joseph Shmuel (1837) found Purim unobserved; by the late 19th c. it was widely kept.

halacha_index.summary_he: פורים הוא אחד החגים הפופולריים ביותר; שמותיו נגזרים מהמן. בתענית אסתר מכינות נשים חלווה "חסידו" (קמח קלוי, חמאה, דבש או סוכר, אגוזים) ולבש דק. סעודת הערב היא מרק קמח "קוטה חשיל" עם דבש, כשקרובים מוזמנים וסעודות נשלחות לנזקקים.

halacha_index.summary: Rice is eaten on Pesach but not on the first two days (Yom Tov); it is cooked from Chol HaMoed. R. Avigdor Yunaev (Jerusalem) explains this as deference to Caucasian Ashkenazim at shared seders, extended to both diaspora Yom Tov days.
common_practices: No rice on the first two days
Rice on Chol HaMoed
halacha_index.source: Interview with R. Avigdor Yunaev, Evreiskii zhurnal, 29 Mar 2018 (Russian); Chabad.org, '19 Facts About the Mountain Jews'
halacha_index.review_notes: The custom is consistently reported; the explanation is one rabbi's view. Practice in Israel (one or two days) is undocumented.

references.title: The Jews Who Rode with Daggers
19 Facts About the “Mountain Jews” - Chabad.org
Для кого рис в Песах не хамец - Сила Теилим

halacha_index.summary_he: אורז נאכל בפסח אך לא בשני הימים הראשונים (יום טוב); הוא מבושל מחול המועד. הרב אביגדור יונייב (ירושלים) מסביר זאת כהתחשבות באשכנזים הקווקזיים בסדרים משותפים, שהורחבה לשני ימי הטוב של הגולה.

halacha_index.summary: The Mountain Jewish community of Azerbaijan avoids pickles, sugar and cheese on Pesach; JTA (2021) puts it at about 8,000 people, most of Azerbaijan's Jews. Yaniv Naftaliev (Israel community leader) explains this as dating from when no rabbinically supervised factories existed. In 19th-c. Vartashen: no dried fish or sweets for eight days, and many would not eat another family's matzah.
common_practices: No pickled foods, sugar or cheese

variants.practice: No lamb shank on the seder plate.
No dried fish or sweets.

halacha_index.source: JTA/Zman Yisrael, 'בלי חמוצים, סוכר או גבינות' (Hebrew, 27 Mar 2021); Dymshits 1999
halacha_index.review_notes: This is a stringency based on supervision; its application today is a rabbinic question.
halacha_index.summary_he: קהילת יהודי ההרים באזרבייג'ן נמנעת ממלפפונים חמוצים, סוכר וגבינה בפסח; סוכנות JTA (2021) מעריכה אותם בכ-8,000 איש, רוב יהודי אזרבייג'ן. יניב נפתלייב (מנהיג הקהילה בישראל) מסביר זאת כמתארך מזמן שלא היו מפעלים בהשגחה רבנית. בוורטשן של המאה ה-19: אין דגים מיובשים או מתוקים שמונה ימים, ורבים לא אכלו מצה של משפחה אחרת.

halacha_index.summary: Wheat is bought from a threshing floor untouched by rain and stored in a new clay jug, then hand-sorted 30 days before Pesach. The mill is cleaned and inspected by the rabbi, and the flour kept from the sun. Only men (15-20) bake, each with one fixed task, all saying it is 'for matzah'.
common_practices: Dough in 2.75-funt portions
Water drawn the day before
A new tandoor not used for ordinary bread
Under-baked matzah may not be returned to the oven
New knives
halacha_index.source: Dymshits 1999, 'Pesakh', quoting Bezhanov (1894) (Russian)
halacha_index.review_notes: Historical, single community. The same source describes kashering tinned copper by boiling with a clay-sealed rim.
halacha_index.summary_he: קונים חיטה מגורן שלא ירד עליה גשם ומאחסנים אותה בכד חימר חדש, ומיינים אותה ביד שלושים יום לפני פסח. הרב מנקה ובודק את הטחנה, והקמח נשמר מהשמש. רק גברים (15-20) אופים, כל אחד במשימה קבועה אחת, וכולם אומרים שזה "לשם מצה".

halacha_index.summary: The Haggadah is read in Hebrew at the first seder and in Juhuri translation at the second. A thorny plant (a blue thorn also used as an amulet) is eaten with the maror. For the plagues, wine is poured ten times into a broken clay vessel with ash and an eggshell.
common_practices: Home-made wine
Haroset of pounded fruit
Thorn dish 'kisani burochoi'

variants.practice: A seder melody composed by R. Avraham b. Chanukah, heir of R. Eliyahu b. Mishael.

halacha_index.source: Dymshits 1999, 'Pesakh' (Russian)
halacha_index.review_notes: Gorskie.ru describes the thorn dish as nettle-based; sources differ on the plant.

Песах: история исхода, свободы и традиции еврейского народа - GORSKIE.ru

halacha_index.summary_he: ההגדה נקראת בעברית בסדר הראשון ובתרגום ליהודית-טאתית (ג'והורי) בשני. צמח קוצני (קוץ כחול המשמש גם קמיע) נאכל עם המרור. בעשר המכות יוצקים יין עשר פעמים לכלי חימר שבור עם אפר וקליפת ביצה.

halacha_index.topic: Nisan: no cemetery visits; 1 Nisan bonfires
halacha_index.summary: No cemetery visits during Pesach and Nisan; Nisan yahrzeits are marked before or after the month. Bonfires are lit on 1 Nisan. Pre-Pesach cleaning starts with the carpets, where meals were eaten.
common_practices: No cemetery in Nisan
Moving Nisan yahrzeits
Bonfires on 1 Nisan
halacha_index.source: JTA (C. Liphshiz, 2021) via STMEGI (Russian); G. Zakharyayev in Vestnik Kavkaza
halacha_index.review_notes: Davidov adds that cemetery visits are forbidden on all Torah festivals.

references.title: Евреи Азербайджана сохраняют многовековые пасхальные традиции
Горские евреи хранят многовековые традиции Песаха - STMEGI

halacha_index.topic_he: ניסן: אין ביקור בבית קברות; מדורות בא' בניסן
halacha_index.summary_he: אין ביקורי בית קברות במשך פסח וניסן; יארצייטים של ניסן מצוינים לפני החודש או אחריו. מדליקים מדורות בא' בניסן. ניקיון לפני פסח מתחיל בשטיחים, שעליהם אכלו.

halacha_index.topic: End of Pesach: grass in the chimney
halacha_index.summary: On the evening of the eighth day, people climbed onto the roof and threw a bunch of fresh grass down the chimney to mark spring.
halacha_index.source: Dymshits 1999, 'Pesakh' (Russian)
halacha_index.review_notes: Single source; place not specified.
halacha_index.summary_he: בערב היום השמיני עלו אנשים לגג והשליכו צרור עשב טרי מטה בארובה לציון האביב.

halacha_index.summary: Mountain Jews (mainly from Krasnaya Sloboda) hold weddings from the end of Pesach (Govgil) until 1 Iyar, considered the most auspicious time. R. Bentsion Zilber notes the Shulchan Aruch keeps mourning until the morning of the 34th day. Because several valid customs exist, he accepts that they may continue.
common_practices: Weddings between Govgil and 1 Iyar

variants.practice: Until 1 Iyar (some say until 1 May).
Govgil as a day for betrothals.

halacha_index.source: Toldot.com Q&A, answer by R. Bentsion Zilber (Russian), citing Shulchan Aruch
halacha_index.review_notes: The end point of Omer mourning is not documented; see gaps.
halacha_index.summary_he: יהודי ההרים (בעיקר מקרסנאיה סלובודה) עורכים חתונות מסוף פסח (גובגיל) עד א' באייר, הנחשב לזמן המוצלח ביותר. הרב בנציון זילבר מציין שהשולחן ערוך שומר על האבלות עד בוקר היום ה-34. מפני שיש כמה מנהגים תקפים, הוא מקבל שאפשר להמשיך בהם.

halacha_index.summary: Lag BaOmer is a 'quiet' minor day with little ritual form (STMEGI, citing Anisimov 1888). Sources disagree on whether the spring bonfire day 'Sha'ame Vassal' is Lag BaOmer.

variants.practice: 'Sha'ame Vassal' is a name for Lag BaOmer.

variants.subgroup: Russian anthropologists (Yehuda Cherni, Vsevolod Miller, per Hadassah 2008) and Dymshits
variants.practice: Spring bonfires (Majalis, Nyugdi, Quba) are a separate pre-Jewish spring custom; in Krasnaya Sloboda (1997) only pre-bat-mitzvah girls took part.

halacha_index.source: STMEGI, 'Lag ba-Omer u gorskikh evreev' (Russian); Hadassah 2008; Dymshits 1999
halacha_index.review_notes: The NLI Piyut site lists a Mountain Jewish recording of 'Bar Yochai'.

references.title: Лаг ба-Омер у горских евреев: традиции, история и современность - STMEGI

halacha_index.summary_he: ל"ג בעומר הוא יום משני "שקט" עם מעט צורת טקס (STMEGI, בציטוט אניסימוב 1888). המקורות חלוקים אם יום המדורות של האביב "שעמה ואסל" הוא ל"ג בעומר.

halacha_index.summary: Shavuot is 'Asalta' (the sweet one), when sweets are eaten. Rabbis and literate men read Torah and Prophets all night in the synagogue. In the morning they immerse in the synagogue-courtyard mikveh, then pray and read the 613 commandments. Families bereaved that year are visited.
common_practices: All-night reading
Morning mikveh
Reading the 613 mitzvot

variants.practice: Repeated on the second day.

halacha_index.source: Dymshits 1999, 'Shavuot' (Russian)
halacha_index.review_notes: Dymshits notes Shavuot became less popular in the Soviet period.
halacha_index.summary_he: שבועות הוא "אסלטה" (המתוק), שבו אוכלים ממתקים. רבנים ואנשים משכילים קוראים תורה ונביאים כל הלילה בבית הכנסת. בבוקר טובלים במקווה שבחצר בית הכנסת, ואחר כך מתפללים וקוראים את תרי"ג המצוות. מבקרים משפחות שאבלו באותה שנה.

halacha_index.summary: Tisha B'Av is one of the most important days. Candles are lit in every home and Eicha is read in dim synagogues, sitting on the floor; people sleep in their clothes. After morning prayers, people go to the cemetery barefoot or in non-leather shoes to visit family graves with Hashkava and Kaddish, and give generous tzedakah.
common_practices: Home candles
Floor-sitting for Eicha
Cemetery visit to family graves

variants.practice: Thousands, including emigrants, gather; most explained the day as mourning for Mayrom (Miriam) and her seven martyred sons rather than the Temple.
Explicitly mourning Jerusalem: Eicha, Job, ashes, barefoot.
Both the Temple and Mayrom's sons are mourned.

halacha_index.source: Davidov, Mudretsy Kavkaza, 'Suruni 9 Ava (Obychai i traditsii)' (Russian); Dymshits 1999
halacha_index.review_notes: Davidov: if 9 Av falls on Shabbat, the fast moves to Sunday.

references.title: Религиозная жизнь и обычаи горских евреев / Главы / Библиотека / Еврейская интернет библиотека
מרכז המורשת הבינלאומי ליהדות קווקז » מסורת ומורשת רוחנית

halacha_index.summary_he: תשעה באב הוא אחד הימים החשובים ביותר. מדליקים נרות בכל בית וקוראים איכה בבתי כנסת עמומים, בישיבה על הרצפה; ישנים בבגדים. אחרי תפילת הבוקר הולכים אנשים לבית הקברות יחפים או בנעליים שאינן מעור לבקר בקברי המשפחה עם השכבה וקדיש, ונותנים צדקה בנדיבות.

halacha_index.summary: From 1 Av, for two weeks: no meat, no river or sea bathing (washing for Shabbat is allowed), no laundry, no celebrations, no new clothes. Mourning ends the day after the fast, when weddings are held.
common_practices: No meat from 1 Av
Weddings right after the fast
halacha_index.source: Davidov, 'Suruni 9 Ava (Obychai i traditsii)' (Russian)
halacha_index.review_notes: Single source. 'Two weeks' from 1 Av runs past 9 Av; the end point needs checking.
halacha_index.summary_he: מא' באב, במשך שבועיים: אין בשר, אין רחיצה בנהר או בים (רחיצה לשבת מותרת), אין כביסה, אין שמחות, אין בגדים חדשים. האבלות מסתיימת ביום שאחרי הצום, כשעורכים חתונות.

halacha_index.summary: The shochet is the central religious figure; in villages any shochet is called 'rabbi'. In 19th-c. Quba, each quarter-community ate only meat slaughtered by its own shochet. In the late Soviet period, poultry was slaughtered in synagogue courtyards.
common_practices: Meat from one's own community shochet
Strict separation of meat and dairy

variants.practice: Pork, horse and rabbit forbidden; meat and dairy kept apart.
variants.source: KBR regional ethnography page 'Evrei: traditsii i obychai' (Russian)

variants.practice: Most buy kosher meat and keep separate dishes; more secular families may eat out non-kosher.

halacha_index.source: Dymshits 1999, 'Ravvinat i ravviny', citing I. Chorny (Russian)
halacha_index.summary_he: השוחט הוא הדמות הדתית המרכזית; בכפרים כל שוחט נקרא "רבי". בקובה של המאה ה-19 אכלה כל קהילת רובע רק בשר ששחט השוחט שלה. בסוף התקופה הסובייטית נשחטו עופות בחצרות בתי הכנסת.

halacha_index.summary: Milah is on the eighth day, even on Shabbat. It is postponed for illness, and if a sibling died after circumcision, but not for mourning. The night before, 'Brit-Yitzchak' is held: Torah study by father, relatives and friends (Davidov notes it has become a festive meal). Ten men are present.
common_practices: Mother hands the baby to the grandmother, who hands him to the sandak
All rise and say 'Baruch ha-ba'
One large and several small candles
Kosher wine on the baby's lips
Periah and metzitzah required
Name given in the blessing
Tehillim at the bed's head against the evil eye
Meal with wine, fish, meat and fruit
Gifts to guests: socks and handkerchiefs for men, headscarves for women

variants.practice: Often performed by a physician.

halacha_index.source: Davidov, Mudretsy Kavkaza, 'Brit-mila (Obychai i traditsii)' (Russian)
halacha_index.review_notes: The Encyclopedia of World Cultures says 'seventh day', which conflicts with Davidov; see disputes.

references.title: Mountain Jews | Encyclopedia.com

halacha_index.summary_he: המילה ביום השמיני, גם בשבת. היא נדחית בגלל מחלה, ואם אח מת אחרי מילה, אך לא בגלל אבלות. בלילה שלפני כן נערכת "ברית יצחק": לימוד תורה בידי האב, קרובים וחברים (דבידוב מציין שהיא הפכה לסעודה חגיגית). עשרה גברים נוכחים.

halacha_index.summary: Boys are named at the milah, girls at the Torah on the first Shabbat after birth. Names usually follow grandparents and deceased relatives, in Juhuri forms: Moshe→Mishi, Yehuda→Evdo, Binyamin→Beneimi, Leah→Lio, Tzipora→Sipro.
common_practices: After the first-year memorial, a granddaughter under 12 may receive the deceased grandmother's name as an added name
halacha_index.source: Davidov, 'Brit-mila' and 'Traur' (Russian); Encyclopedia of World Cultures
halacha_index.summary_he: בנים נקראים בשמם במילה, בנות בתורה בשבת הראשונה אחרי הלידה. השמות הולכים בדרך כלל אחרי סבים וקרובים שנפטרו, בצורות ג'והורי: משה→מישי, יהודה→אבדו, בנימין→בנאימי, לאה→ליו, צפורה→סיפרו.

halacha_index.summary: At a bar mitzvah, women, who otherwise did not enter the synagogue hall, came in holding lit candles to hear the Torah reading. The Juhuri term reported is 'tefilinvenim'.
common_practices: Women enter with candles
halacha_index.source: Davidov, 'Chtenie Tory' (Russian); STMEGI, 'Traditsii i religioznye obychai: dehmerd'
halacha_index.review_notes: The term comes from one page not opened by the lead researcher.

references.title: Чтение Торы (Обычаи и традиции) / Главы / Библиотека / Еврейская интернет библиотека

halacha_index.summary_he: בבר מצווה נכנסו נשים, שמלבד זאת לא נכנסו לאולם בית הכנסת, כשהן מחזיקות נרות דולקים, כדי לשמוע את קריאת התורה. המונח בג'והורי המדווח הוא "תפילינבנים".

halacha_index.summary: Sequence: matchmaking; the 'tonoi' contract (tnaim) setting the date and a bride-payment for the trousseau; the dowry listed by the rabbi with two witnesses; then celebrations starting separately in both houses. On the wedding day bride and groom fast and immerse 'as on Yom Kippur'. The bride must go to the mikveh: 'a bride who has not immersed is forbidden to the groom'.
common_practices: Velvet chuppah on four poles in the bride's courtyard before nightfall
Groom wears a tallit
Rabbi reads the ketubah and performs kiddushin and nissuin
Groom covers the bride's head with a scarf and breaks a glass
Candles, zurna and drums
Sweets and rice thrown
Money placed in the dancing bride's hand

variants.practice: Groom bathes in the river; ash placed on his forehead for Jerusalem; Psalm 137 sung.
'Mikveh' by bathing in a river or bathhouse, depending on season.
variants.source: Yu. I. Murzakhanov, 'Svadebnye obryady gorskikh evreev Severnogo Kavkaza' (CyberLeninka)

halacha_index.source: Davidov, Mudretsy Kavkaza, 'Sem'ya (Obychai i traditsii)' (Russian)
halacha_index.review_notes: Historical early marriage and polygamy (EJE: Rabbeinu Gershom's ban was not accepted) are not current practice.
halacha_index.summary_he: הסדר: שידוך; חוזה ה"טונוי" (תנאים) הקובע את התאריך ותשלום כלה לנדוניה; הנדוניה שהרב רושם בפני שני עדים; ואחר כך חגיגות המתחילות בנפרד בשני הבתים. ביום החתונה צמים החתן והכלה וטובלים "כמו ביום כיפור". הכלה חייבת ללכת למקווה: "כלה שלא טבלה אסורה לחתן".

halacha_index.summary: Mikveh use is documented for brides before the wedding and for men on Shavuot morning. A new mikveh was built beside the active Gilyaki synagogue in Krasnaya Sloboda.
common_practices: Bridal immersion required
halacha_index.source: Davidov, 'Sem'ya'; Dymshits 1999 (Russian)
halacha_index.review_notes: No niddah practice was found; see gaps.

references.title: Семья (Обычаи и традиции) / Главы / Библиотека / Еврейская интернет библиотека

halacha_index.summary_he: השימוש במקווה מתועד לכלות לפני החתונה ולגברים בבוקר שבועות. מקווה חדש נבנה ליד בית הכנסת הפעיל של הגילקים בקרסנאיה סלובודה.

halacha_index.summary: The body is laid on the floor, covered with a sheet, with a candle or lamp, and Tehillim is read beside it. An accident victim is not brought into the house. Tahara is done in a trough, and the body is dressed in 'akhireti' (white linen shroud sewn with linen thread). A man is covered with a tallit with torn tzitzit, a woman with a large shawl.
common_practices: Seven stops reciting Psalm 91 on the way to the cemetery (Derbent to Nalchik)
Bier set at least four steps before the cemetery, feet west, for hesped and Kaddish
A coin paid for the plot
Women and the deceased's children do not attend the burial
Burial about 1.5 m deep, feet west, boards above
Earth from the grave bottom given to mourners
No talk over the fresh grave
Mourners leave last, barefoot or with earth in their shoes
Return by a different road

variants.practice: Seven hakafot for a man; seven Psalms for a woman or child.
Keriah after burial in Nalchik; elsewhere during preparations or at the door.

halacha_index.source: A. Davidov, Mudretsy Kavkaza, 'Traur (Obychai i traditsii)', reprinted gorskie.ru 4 Aug 2015 (Russian)
halacha_index.review_notes: The Encyclopedia of World Cultures confirms same-day burial with the whole community attending.

references.title: Траур (Обычаи и традиции) / Главы / Библиотека / Еврейская интернет библиотека

halacha_index.summary_he: הגופה מונחת על הרצפה, מכוסה בסדין, עם נר או מנורה, ואומרים תהילים לצדה. קורבן תאונה אינו מובא לבית. הטהרה נעשית בעביט, והגופה לבושה "אחירטי" (תכריכי פשתן לבנים תפורים בחוט פשתן). גבר מכוסה בטלית עם ציציות קרועות, אישה בצעיף גדול.

halacha_index.summary: Shiva counts from the burial, with a candle burning for seven days. Mourners sit on the floor, women and men in separate rooms. Every household sends food for the mourners' meal ('Borokho'): hard-boiled eggs, beans, plain rice, fish. Meat and vodka are served when the deceased died old. On day 7 the rabbi ends shiva and the family visits the grave, women first; the same is done on day 30 ('Chulya') and at the year ('Sal'). Sources differ on whether the second memorial falls on day 30 or day 40.
common_practices: Rabbi breaks three lavash ('Mesi')
Minyan at home for seven days
Mourners skip Monday/Thursday Torah readings, Purim and Chanukah
Mourners usually go up to the Torah on the fourth Shabbat, buying maftir
Seat change and haircut after 30 days
No weddings or festive visits for a year
No black clothing
No mourning for an infant under 31 days

variants.practice: Memorials at 7 days, 40 days and 1 year; mourning called 'yos'.
The second memorial falls on day 30 ('Chulya').

halacha_index.source: Davidov, 'Traur' (Russian)
halacha_index.review_notes: Day 30 (Davidov) versus day 40 (ethnography): both are recorded.
halacha_index.summary_he: השבעה נמנית מהקבורה, כשנר דולק שבעה ימים. האבלים יושבים על הרצפה, נשים וגברים בחדרים נפרדים. כל משק בית שולח אוכל לסעודת האבלים ("בורוחו"): ביצים קשות, שעועית, אורז פשוט, דג. בשר וודקה מוגשים כשהנפטר מת זקן. ביום השביעי הרב מסיים את השבעה והמשפחה מבקרת בקבר, הנשים תחילה; כך עושים ביום השלושים ("חולייה") ובשנה ("סל"). המקורות חלוקים אם ההזכרה השנייה חלה ביום ה-30 או ביום ה-40.

halacha_index.summary: Kaddish is said for 11 months, ten times daily (four 'Al Yisrael' and six 'Yatom'); it resumes on the evening of the 30th day before the first anniversary. The first 'Sal' is counted 12 months from burial, later ones from the date of death. The yahrzeit is called 'taanit' because children are obliged to fast for their parents. Candles are lit at home and in synagogue, with Mishnah, Tehillim and Kaddish, and an aliyah on the Shabbat.
common_practices: Food brought to synagogue for ancestors' yahrzeits
Gravestone by the first year
Evening services end with Hashkava for the year's dead
halacha_index.source: Davidov, 'Traur' (Russian)
halacha_index.review_notes: A first anniversary on Shabbat, Yom Tov, Purim or 9 Av is moved 'на день вперёд'; the direction (earlier or later) is ambiguous.

references.title: Траур (Обычаи и традиции) / Главы / Библиотека / Еврейская интернет библиотека
Обычаи и традиции горских евреев: траур - GORSKIE.ru

halacha_index.summary_he: אומרים קדיש 11 חודשים, עשר פעמים ביום (ארבעה "על ישראל" ושישה "יתום"); הוא חוזר בערב היום השלושים לפני יום השנה הראשון. ה"סל" הראשון נמנה 12 חודשים מהקבורה, ואלה שאחריו מיום הפטירה. היארצייט נקרא "תענית" כי הילדים חייבים לצום על הוריהם. מדליקים נרות בבית ובבית הכנסת, עם משנה, תהילים וקדיש, ועלייה לתורה בשבת.

unique_minhagim.name: Govgil (גבגיל; 'govlei geulah')
unique_minhagim.description: The day after Pesach. That night new bread and sweet flatbreads are baked; families spend the day outdoors picnicking with relatives and guests. A bowl of sweets or fruit is ringed with young grass and topped with about five gold items or coins. A blessing is sung: 'Imishev shev Govgili, sabah ruz Donili…', rendered by STMEGI as 'Today we are freed from our chains, and tomorrow, with the help of the Almighty and the prophet Daniel, may we all be fed and healthy in Jerusalem!' A traditional betrothal time; in Israel celebrated publicly (e.g. Kiryat Yam) and compared to Mimouna.
unique_minhagim.source: STMEGI, 'Govgil' i Mimuna'; STMEGI, 'Pesakh: Prazdnik chistoi dushi'; JTA 2021

references.title: Govgil
Песах: Праздник Чистой Души - STMEGI

unique_minhagim.description_he: היום שאחרי פסח. באותו לילה אופים לחם חדש ולחמניות מתוקות; משפחות מבלות את היום בחוץ בפיקניק עם קרובים ואורחים. קערת ממתקים או פירות מוקפת עשב צעיר ובראשה כחמישה פריטי זהב או מטבעות. שרים ברכה: "אימישב שב גובגילי, סבה רוז דונילי…", שמתורגמת בידי STMEGI "היום משוחררים מכבלינו, ומחר, בעזרת הקב"ה והנביא דניאל, נהיה כולנו שבעים ובריאים בירושלים!". זמן אירוסין מסורתי; בישראל נחגג בפומבי (למשל בקריית ים) ומושווה למימונה.

unique_minhagim.name: Bonfires of 1 Nisan
unique_minhagim.description: Bonfires on Rosh Chodesh Nisan, with shashlik according to gorskie.ru.
unique_minhagim.description_he: מדורות בראש חודש ניסן, עם שישליק לפי gorskie.ru.

unique_minhagim.name: Bilingual seder
unique_minhagim.description: Haggadah in Hebrew on the first night and in Juhuri on the second.
unique_minhagim.description_he: הגדה בעברית בלילה הראשון ובג'והורי בשני.

unique_minhagim.name: Shev-Idor
unique_minhagim.description: A folk 'night of Idor' before spring: the housewife presents a tray of fruit saved through the year, the master blesses and all pray for a fruitful year. Dymshits compares it to Tu BiShvat; its date is unrecorded.
unique_minhagim.description_he: "ליל אידור" עממי לפני האביב: עקרת הבית מציגה מגש פירות ששמרה כל השנה, בעל הבית מברך והכול מתפללים לשנה פוריה. דימשיץ משווה אותו לט"ו בשבט; תאריכו אינו מתועד.

unique_minhagim.name: Machzor Ohalei Yaakov
unique_minhagim.description: High Holiday machzor with commentary by R. Yaakov Yitzchaki: vol. 1 Selichot/Rosh Hashana (Jerusalem 1908), vol. 2 Yom Kippur (1910). Planned parts for the festivals and fasts remained in manuscript.
unique_minhagim.description_he: מחזור לימים הנוראים עם פירוש של רבי יעקב יצחקי: כרך א' סליחות/ראש השנה (ירושלים 1908), כרך ב' יום כיפור (1910). החלקים המתוכננים למועדים ולתעניות נשארו בכתב יד.

unique_minhagim.name: Juhuri siddur 'Kol Tefilla'
unique_minhagim.description: First Juhuri prayer book, Vilna 1909, with parallel Hebrew, translated by Asaf Pinkhasov of Derbent.
unique_minhagim.description_he: סידור התפילה הג'והורי הראשון, וילנה 1909, עם עברית מקבילה, בתרגום אסף פינחסוב מדרבנט.

unique_minhagim.name: Local piyyut and recordings
unique_minhagim.description: Piyyutim by Elisha b. Shmuel ha-Katan of Aba-Sava (three published by I. Chorny). The NLI holds Caucasus-tradition recordings of 'Yom Zeh Mechubad', 'Lecha Dodi' and 'Bar Yochai'.

references.title: Религиозная жизнь и обычаи горских евреев / Главы / Библиотека / Еврейская интернет библиотека

unique_minhagim.description_he: פיוטים של אלישע בן שמואל הקטן מאבא-סבא (שלושה פורסמו בידי י' צ'ורני). הספרייה הלאומית מחזיקה הקלטות ממסורת הקווקז של "יום זה מכובד", "לכה דודי" ו"בר יוחאי".

gaps: Shabbat candle lighting, Kabbalat Shabbat, Kiddush, seudot and Havdalah: no community-specific source
End of Omer mourning and haircut customs
Minor fasts other than the Vartashen Rosh Hashana fasts
Tefillin and tzitzit (only an anecdote that elders wore a tallit katan)
Torah pronunciation and cantillation: NLI recordings exist but no written description
Calendar and zmanim: no documented offsets, so parameters are empty
Bakashot: no evidence of a tradition
disputes: Brit milah day: Encyclopedia of World Cultures says the seventh day; Davidov and halacha say the eighth (probably an error in the encyclopedia).
Memorial day: 30th (Davidov) versus 40th (Encyclopedia of World Cultures).
Chanukah: barely remembered (Dymshits) versus the major winter holiday (Encyclopedia of World Cultures).
Sukkah dwelling: Kiddush only (Dymshits) versus seven days (Bezhanov, Vartashen).
Tisha B'Av: mourning for Mayrom's sons (1990s Krasnaya Sloboda informants) versus the Temple (Bezhanov; Davidov includes both).
Sha'ame Vassal: Lag BaOmer (Brooklyn activist) versus a separate spring custom (ethnographers).
Shabbat weapons: rabbis banned weapons in synagogue on Shabbat versus daggers never removed (Dymshits reports both).
needs_rabbinic_review: Rice on one or two days of Pesach in Israel
End point of the restrictions from Rosh Chodesh Av
Govgil-to-1 Iyar weddings versus Shulchan Aruch
Children's yahrzeit fast ('taanit') on days when fasting is not done
Pesach sugar, cheese and pickle restrictions where certified products exist
Folk customs (Elijah night, Shev-Idor, Aravo divination) to be presented as ethnography, not halacha
